cards.text: This one's a letter from James, who calls himself “a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ” and writes “To the twelve tribes of the Dispersion”. His whole hello is one word: “Greetings.” That's ALL the small talk you're getting, friend.
Then James goes straight to trials of many kinds and tells his brothers how to look at them.

cards.question: When his brothers run into trials of many kinds, what does James tell them to consider it?

cards.text: Pure JOY in trials? Friend, when a batch burns, I don't throw a party, but James gives a reason.

cards.question: James tells his brothers to count trials as joy, because the testing of their faith develops ___.

cards.text: Then James says, “Allow perseverance to finish its work…” Friend, I've pulled a batch out early, and it's gooey in the middle EVERY time.

cards.question: When perseverance finishes its work, what does James say his brothers will be?

cards.text: Next, James talks to anyone who lacks wisdom. I once stood in front of an oven for ten minutes waiting on a batch, and the oven was OFF, so yeah, he's talking to me.

cards.question: According to James, anyone who lacks wisdom should ask ___.
James says God gives generously to all without finding fault.

cards.text: But here's the catch: James says ask in faith, without doubting. Then he paints a picture of the person who doubts.

cards.question: What picture does James use for the person who doubts?

answers.text: A wave tossed by the wind
A sheep lost from the flock
A lamp hidden under a bowl

cards.question: James says the person who asks while doubting should still expect to receive something from the Lord.

cards.text: James calls the doubter a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways. That's me at the topping shelf going chocolate chips, no, sprinkles, no, WAIT, chocolate chips.
Next, James says the brother in humble circumstances should exult in his high position. The humble brother gets told he's sitting HIGH, and friend, I like where this is going.

cards.question: James says the humble brother should exult in his high position, but the one who is rich should exult in his ___ position.
James compares the rich man to a flower of the field. Why does James say the rich man should exult in his low position?

answers.text: Because he must give it all away
Because his riches are a test

cards.text: The sun rises with scorching heat, and the flower falls. So too, James says, the rich man will fade away in the midst of his pursuits.

Then James circles back to trials: the man who perseveres under trial is blessed, and once he has stood the test, he will receive the crown of life. A CROWN, friend, and I thought my tall white chef's hat was fancy!

cards.question: James says God has promised the crown of life to those who love Him.
When it comes to being tempted, James says it's fine to say, “God is tempting me.”
James says God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does He tempt anyone. So where does James say each person's temptation comes from?

cards.text: James says each one is lured away and enticed by his own desires. Nobody DRAGGED me face-first into the chocolate chips, friend, because I hopped in myself, gold base and all.

cards.question: James says desire conceives and gives birth to sin. What does he say happens when sin is full-grown?

answers.text: It fades away on its own

cards.text: Then James says, “Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers.” BELOVED, from the man whose whole hello was one word!

cards.question: God tempts no one, and James says every good and perfect gift is from ___.

cards.text: Every gift comes down from the Father of the heavenly lights, with whom there is no change or shifting shadow. My oven runs hot one batch and cold the next, but God never changes on you, friend.

cards.question: James says the Father chose to give us birth. What does James say He did it through?

cards.text: He did it so that we would be a kind of firstfruits of His creation. CHOSEN, friend, and after years in the back of a junk drawer, being chosen still gets me EVERY time.
